body:
Root-caused and fixed the concrete half of a founder real-time security complaint
("logged out when i shouldnt be"). IDUNA commit 65fb9a0.

Found: /admin's iduna_session cookie + embedded JWT both had a hard 8h expiry with
no refresh-on-activity. A still-active admin session would silently bounce to
/admin/login on the first request after the 8h mark, with zero explanation shown —
this reads exactly like an "unexpected" logout during a long working session, and
this box's own history (many late-night/overnight work sessions visible throughout
BACKLOG.md timestamps) makes an 8h continuous admin session plausible.

Fixed: RequireCookieAuth(keys, loginURL, sessionTTL) now does sliding-expiration
refresh — once less than half of sessionTTL remains on the current token, it
transparently re-signs the claims with a fresh full-TTL expiry and sets a new
cookie on the response, so continuous activity never hits the wall. Shared
AdminSessionTTL constant (8h) added to handlers package so admin_login.go's
initial issuance and the middleware's refresh window can't drift apart. Only
consumer of RequireCookieAuth is /admin (verified via grep) — web_ceremony.go and
shankpit_auth.go use separate, intentionally short-lived (5min) one-shot exchange
cookies through a different code path, unaffected by this change.

4 new tests (fresh session = no refresh, stale session = refreshed with later exp
+ claims preserved, sessionTTL=0 = refresh disabled, expired session = redirects).
go test ./... green across all of IDUNA.

Honest scope gap, not resolved: the founder's complaint didn't specify which
login they meant (admin back office vs. WordPress/EDIS vs. SSH vs. something
else) - this fixes a real, verified bug in the one session mechanism most likely
to match "was using something for a while, then randomly logged out," but can't
be confirmed as *the* root cause without founder confirmation. Flagged in
BACKLOG.md S191 rather than claimed as definitively resolved.

Also ran a read-only security sweep (no code changes, findings only): `last`
shows all root logins from a consistent 174.210.22x.x/24-ish address range
(same-ISP dynamic-IP pattern, no unrecognized foreign IPs), no crontab entries,
free memory/swap healthy (9.3GB available, no dmesg OOM events), fail2ban active.
Could not query fail2ban ban-list or read /var/log/auth.log — both require sudo,
consistent with this box's existing no-passwordless-sudo constraint documented
elsewhere in BACKLOG.md (S30-02, S23-01, etc.). No signs of external intrusion
found within what's readable without elevated privileges.

PARENA-native tooling ("using parena tools" / "build the tools in parena") was
explicitly requested for this investigation but grep.prn/sed.prn/awk.prn are
confirmed still unbuilt per S190-01's own tracked remaining scope (the
regex/nfa.prn engine they'd call now exists and works, the CLI wrapper tools
don't yet) - used standard shell tools for this time-sensitive pass instead,
per the tradeoff already flagged in the observation itself.

⚓ ☃
title: S191-02: admin session sliding-expiration fix
